response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT r.ordervault, o.orderflow, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY r.ordervault, o.orderflow), s AS (SELECT ordervault, orderflow, record_count, record_count * 1.0 / SUM(record_count) OVER (PARTITION BY orderflow) AS share FROM c), d AS (SELECT ordervault, orderflow, record_count, share, AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY orderflow) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT ordervault, orderflow, record_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_status_avg FROM d WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share_minus_status_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique per order (as documented), so the inner join does not duplicate risk/margin records.
The status average is the unweighted mean of the shares across the (ordervault, orderflow) combinations within that status, computed after the inner join.
